title: HMC Capital Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: A person who is an employee, officer or director of a Group Entity (which includes Home Consortium Limited, its subsidiaries, and managed LPTs such as HCW) and includes Senior Executives. Subject to the Blackout Period ban, the short-term trading and short-position bans, the hedging ban on unvested/restricted incentive securities, and the standard pre-approval and associate-coverage obligations.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of a Group Entity. Distinguished for Pre-approval Request routing (Chair and Group Company Secretary, in consultation with the Group CEO) and for the 2-business-day post-trade notification duty.

tiers.name: Senior Executives
tiers.description: The CEO and CFO of a Group Entity, all direct reports to the Group CEO, other Group key management personnel (AASB 124), or any Employee the Board designates as a Senior Executive. Distinguished for the margin lending consent requirement (section 8) and the 2-business-day post-trade notification duty.

tiers.name: Group Chief Executive Officer
tiers.description: The Chief Executive Officer of Home Consortium Limited; distinguished as a Pre-approval Request approver for other Employees and Directors, and distinguished for its own Pre-approval Requests and margin lending consent requests being routed instead to the Chair and Group Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Chair
tiers.description: The Chair of the Company; distinguished as an approver of Pre-approval Requests from the Group CEO and Group Company Secretary, and distinguished for its own Pre-approval Requests being routed instead to the Group CEO and Group Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Group Company Secretary
tiers.description: The Company Secretary of Home Consortium Limited; a routine Pre-approval Request approver alongside the Group CEO or Chair, and distinguished for its own Pre-approval Requests being routed instead to the Chair and Group CEO.

tiers.name: Designated Staff Members
tiers.description: Employees with access to sensitive information about the Group's trading positions in Third Party Securities (e.g. research, M&A knowledge, fund management involvement); the Group CEO, the CEO's direct reports, and additional nominated staff. Must check, and if listed obtain pre-approval before trading in, securities on the Restricted List.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: A Director's or Employee's spouse, children and other family members, and any trusts, companies, nominees and other persons over whom the Director or Employee has, or may be expected to have, investment control or influence.

definitions.hedging_definition: entering into transactions or arrangements, including by way of derivatives or similar financial products, which operate to limit the economic risk relating to HMC Capital Group Securities granted under an employee, executive or director incentive plan or as part of the Employee's remuneration, which either have not vested or have vested but remain subject to a holding lock or other restriction on dealing under the terms of the plan

windows.end_anchor: 1 business day after the release of the half year accounts to the ASX
1 business day after the release of the annual accounts to the ASX

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Group Board (including in consultation with the Board of a Group Entity) may declare a Blackout Period at any time in its absolute discretion and without prior notice, for any one or more HMC Capital Group Securities, notified by email once declared. The Group Company Secretary may also notify additional trading restrictions from time to time (e.g. where a Group Entity or LPT is involved in a significant transaction), which Employees must abide by. Neither is stated to be confidential, in contrast to a rejected Pre-approval Request, which must be kept confidential.

rules.detail: HMC Capital Group Securities expressly includes 'Financial Products issued over or in respect of' the underlying shares/units 'which are able to be traded on a financial market', and Financial Products is defined broadly (swaps, futures, CFDs, spread bets, options, warrants, depositary receipts or other derivatives). Dealing in such a product is therefore ordinary Trading, subject to the standard pre-approval process and the Blackout Period ban.
rules.evidence: Financial Products means any structured financial products, swaps, futures contracts, contracts for difference, spread bets, options, warrants, depositary receipts or other derivatives over or related to the performance of any HMC Capital Group Securities.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on entering transactions or arrangements, including by way of derivatives, that limit the economic risk relating to incentive-plan or remuneration securities that have not yet vested.
rules.evidence: entering into transactions or arrangements, including by way of derivatives or similar financial products, which operate to limit the economic risk relating to HMC Capital Group Securities granted under an employee, executive or director incentive plan or as part of the Employee's remuneration, which either have not vested or have vested but remain subject to a holding lock or other restriction on dealing under the terms of the plan

rules.detail: The same ban extends to incentive-plan or remuneration securities that have vested but remain subject to a holding lock or other dealing restriction under the plan's terms.
rules.evidence: entering into transactions or arrangements, including by way of derivatives or similar financial products, which operate to limit the economic risk relating to HMC Capital Group Securities granted under an employee, executive or director incentive plan or as part of the Employee's remuneration, which either have not vested or have vested but remain subject to a holding lock or other restriction on dealing under the terms of the plan

rules.detail: The hedging ban applies only to unvested or still-locked incentive securities; once vested and free of any plan restriction, hedging is not itself banned but is ordinary Trading because a hedging derivative is a Financial Product/HMC Capital Group Security, so the standard pre-approval and Blackout Period regime applies.
rules.evidence: Financial Products means any structured financial products, swaps, futures contracts, contracts for difference, spread bets, options, warrants, depositary receipts or other derivatives over or related to the performance of any HMC Capital Group Securities.

rules.detail: Monetisation structures (e.g. a prepaid forward) are not named, but as a Financial Product related to the performance of HMC Capital Group Securities they are Trading, requiring pre-approval and subject to Blackout Periods; if the structure limits economic risk of an unvested or locked incentive holding it is instead absolutely banned under 3.7(b).
rules.evidence: Financial Products means any structured financial products, swaps, futures contracts, contracts for difference, spread bets, options, warrants, depositary receipts or other derivatives over or related to the performance of any HMC Capital Group Securities.

rules.detail: Broad ban on any Trading, including via derivatives, that enables an Employee to profit from or limit the economic risk of a decrease in the market price of HMC Capital Group Securities, covering both physical short sales and synthetic short positions.
rules.evidence: (short positions) Trading in HMC Capital Group Securities which enable an Employee to profit from or limit the economic risk of a decrease in the market price of HMC Capital Group Securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.

CFDs are expressly named within the Financial Products definition, so a CFD over HMC Capital Group Securities is itself an HMC Capital Group Security requiring ordinary pre-approval; a short CFD position additionally falls within the express short-position ban.
rules.evidence: Financial Products means any structured financial products, swaps, futures contracts, contracts for difference, spread bets, options, warrants, depositary receipts or other derivatives over or related to the performance of any HMC Capital Group Securities.

rules.detail: A Director or Senior Executive may not include their HMC Capital Group Securities in a margin loan portfolio, otherwise Trade pursuant to a margin lending arrangement, or transfer securities into an existing margin loan account, without first obtaining the consent of the Group CEO and Group Company Secretary (or the Chair, if either of those officers is the applicant); consent may be made conditional.
rules.evidence: Directors and Senior Executives may not include their HMC Capital Group Securities in a margin loan portfolio or otherwise Trade in HMC Capital Group Securities pursuant to a margin lending arrangement without first obtaining the consent of the Group Chief Executive Officer and the Group Company Secretary (or, in the case of the Group Chief Executive Officer and the Group Company Secretary, the Chair of the Company).

rules.detail: Section 8's margin lending consent requirement names only Directors and Senior Executives; other Employees are not restricted from margin lending by this Policy.
rules.evidence: Directors and Senior Executives may not include their HMC Capital Group Securities in a margin loan portfolio or otherwise Trade in HMC Capital Group Securities pursuant to a margin lending arrangement without first obtaining the consent of the Group Chief Executive Officer and the Group Company Secretary

rules.detail: Granting security over HMC Capital Group Securities is not separately named; 'a margin lending arrangement' is broad enough to capture any loan secured on the securities carrying a risk of forced sale, so the same section 8 consent should apply to any such encumbrance.
rules.evidence: Directors and Senior Executives may not include their HMC Capital Group Securities in a margin loan portfolio or otherwise Trade in HMC Capital Group Securities pursuant to a margin lending arrangement without first obtaining the consent of the Group Chief Executive Officer and the Group Company Secretary

rules.detail: The section 8 consent requirement is limited to Directors and Senior Executives; other Employees are not restricted from encumbering their securities by this Policy.
rules.evidence: Directors and Senior Executives may not include their HMC Capital Group Securities in a margin loan portfolio or otherwise Trade in HMC Capital Group Securities pursuant to a margin lending arrangement without first obtaining the consent of the Group Chief Executive Officer and the Group Company Secretary

rules.detail: Only a 'margin lending arrangement' is named; a bespoke bank loan secured on the units but not documented as a margin loan is not literally covered by section 8.2's list, but given it carries the identical Blackout-Period forced-sale risk that section 8.1 targets, it should be treated as requiring the same GCEO/Company Secretary (or Chair) consent.
rules.evidence: This is particularly because the terms of the arrangement may require the HMC Capital Group Securities to be sold during a Blackout Period or when the relevant Director or Senior Executive possesses inside information.

rules.detail: Secured financing restrictions in section 8 apply only to Directors and Senior Executives; other Employees are not restricted by this Policy.
rules.evidence: Directors and Senior Executives may not include their HMC Capital Group Securities in a margin loan portfolio or otherwise Trade in HMC Capital Group Securities pursuant to a margin lending arrangement without first obtaining the consent of the Group Chief Executive Officer and the Group Company Secretary

rules.detail: Ban on short-term trading, defined as buying and selling within a 6 month period or entering into other short-term dealings such as forward contracts; carved out for exercising employee options/performance rights at the specified exercise price, and the resulting share sale is not itself regarded as short-term trading.
rules.evidence: Short-term trading includes buying and selling HMC Capital Group Securities within a six month period, and entering into other short-term dealings (e.g. forward contracts). However, the sale of HMC Capital Group Securities that have been converted after exercising options or rights will not be regarded as short-term trading.

clearance.approver: the Group Chief Executive Officer and the Group Company Secretary
clearance.evidence: all Directors and Employees must give a prior written request for pre-approval to the Group Chief Executive Officer and the Group Company Secretary of any proposed Trading in HMC Capital Group Securities

clearance.approver: the Chair and the Group Company Secretary, in consultation with the Group Chief Executive Officer
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 2 business days of execution of the Trade
clearance.evidence: unless the Pre-approval Request is received from a Director where, subject to clause 6.2, it must be approved by the Chair and the Group Company Secretary, in consultation with the Group Chief Executive Officer.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 2 business days of execution of the Trade

clearance.evidence: Group Company Secretary will be approved or rejected by the Chair of the Company and Group Chief Executive Officer.

carve_outs: exercise of employee options or performance rights to acquire HMC Capital Group Securities at the specified exercise price
sale of HMC Capital Group Securities that have been converted after exercising options or rights
short_term.evidence: Short-term trading includes buying and selling HMC Capital Group Securities within a six month period, and entering into other short-term dealings (e.g. forward contracts).

exceptions.evidence: an exercise (but not the sale of HMC Capital Group Securities following exercise) of an option or other right to acquire HMC Capital Group Securities under an employee incentive scheme or the conversion of a convertible HMC Capital Group Security, where the final date for the exercise of the option or right or for the conversion of the HMC Capital Group Security falls during a Blackout Period;

Trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most securityholders in a listed Group Entity or LPT such as a rights or entitlement issue, a security purchase plan, or an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board.

Trading where the beneficial interest in the relevant HMC Capital Group Securities does not change. This includes: a dealing by which the relevant HMC Capital Group Securities are transferred by an Employee from their personal holdings to a superannuation or similar fund of which they are a beneficiary; or the withdrawal of the relevant HMC Capital Group Securities from an employee incentive scheme and the transfer of those securities to the participant's personal holdings or superannuation or similar fund of which they are a beneficiary;

an acquisition of HMC Capital Group Securities under a dividend/distribution reinvestment plan, provided the election to participate in the dividend/distribution reinvestment plan was not made during a Blackout Period or when the Employee was in possession of any inside information;
an Employee accepting a takeover bid or transferring HMC Capital Group Securities under a scheme of arrangement in respect of a Group Entity or LPT;

an involuntary disposal of HMC Capital Group Securities that is the result of a secured lender or financier exercising their rights. However, this does not extend to disposal under a margin lending arrangement where such arrangement is prohibited by this Policy.
an acquisition of HMC Capital Group Securities under a bonus issue made on the same terms to all holders of HMC Capital Group Securities of the same class;

where a Group Entity has an employee incentive scheme with an Employee as a trustee of the scheme, an acquisition of the relevant HMC Capital Group Securities by the Employee in their capacity as a trustee of the scheme;

indirect and incidental Trading that occurs as a consequence of an Employee dealing in securities issued by a managed investment scheme, listed investment company, exchange-traded fund or similar investment vehicle that is managed by a third party and that happens to hold HMC Capital Group Securities as part of its portfolio;

where an Employee is a trustee of a trust, Trading by that trust provided the Employee is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to Trade during a Blackout Period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the relevant Employee;

exceptions.approver: as approved under the procedures set out in this Policy
exceptions.evidence: Trading under a pre-determined investment or divestment plan for which prior written clearance has been provided in accordance with procedures set out in this Policy

exceptions.approver: Group Company Secretary in consultation with the Group Chief Executive Officer (or the Chair, if the Group CEO is the applicant)
exceptions.evidence: severe financial hardship, where the Employee has pressing financial commitments that cannot be satisfied otherwise than by selling HMC Capital Group Securities;

exceptions.approver: Group Company Secretary in consultation with the Group Chief Executive Officer (or the Chair, if the Group CEO is the applicant)
exceptions.evidence: requirements under a court order or court enforceable undertakings or other legal or regulatory requirements.

financing.price_trigger_guidance: A Group Entity may, at its discretion, make any consent granted under section 8.1 conditional upon such terms and conditions that the relevant Group Entity sees fit (for example, specifying the circumstances in which HMC Capital Group Securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
financing_disclosure: Directors and Senior Executives: at inception, before entering into a margin lending arrangement, including their securities in a margin loan portfolio, or transferring securities into an existing margin loan account, to the Group Chief Executive Officer and Group Company Secretary (or the Chair of the Company if either of them is the applicant); consent required before proceeding and may be made conditional.

exemption_authority: The Group Company Secretary, consulting with the Group Chief Executive Officer (or the Chair of the Company if the Group CEO is the applicant), may grant permission to Trade during a Blackout Period in Exceptional Circumstances: severe financial hardship where the securities are the only way to meet a pressing financial commitment, or a court order, court enforceable undertaking, or other legal or regulatory requirement. Permission is entirely discretionary, need not be reasoned, is given in writing, expires 5 trading days from grant unless it specifies otherwise, and may be withdrawn if new information emerges or circumstances change; a refusal must be kept confidential.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Financial Products means any structured financial products, swaps, futures contracts, contracts for difference, spread bets, options, warrants, depositary receipts or other derivatives over or related to the performance of any HMC Capital Group Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is broad enough to expressly capture a bank-written OTC put and call over HCW units as HMC Capital Group Securities in their own right, so the collar's derivative legs sit squarely within the ordinary Trading/pre-approval regime rather than a definitional grey area.

bespoke_clauses.topic: forced sale carve-back for unconsented margin loans
bespoke_clauses.clause: an involuntary disposal of HMC Capital Group Securities that is the result of a secured lender or financier exercising their rights. However, this does not extend to disposal under a margin lending arrangement where such arrangement is prohibited by this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The blanket exclusion for a secured lender's enforcement sale during a Blackout Period only survives if the underlying loan was itself properly consented under section 8 - an unconsented facility loses the benefit of the exclusion, so the bank's loan documentation must be cleared up-front to protect its enforcement rights.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Group Entity may, at its discretion, make any consent granted under section 8.1 conditional upon such terms and conditions that the relevant Group Entity sees fit (for example, specifying the circumstances in which HMC Capital Group Securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Group can dictate the trigger conditions under which the bank may sell the collared units on a margin call as a condition of consenting to the loan.

bespoke_clauses.clause: selling HMC Capital Group Securities to satisfy a call under a margin loan except where the holder of the relevant HMC Capital Group Securities has no control over the sale.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the bank has a unilateral, uninstructed right to sell on a margin call, that sale escapes the section 8 consent requirement and relies instead on the general forced-sale exclusion; a loan giving the executive any discretion over which units are sold needs prior consent for each such sale.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any Employee who holds HMC Capital Group Securities subject to binding restrictions on transfer (either as ASX restricted securities or through voluntary escrow arrangements) must comply with the terms of any applicable escrow arrangements and will be unable to Trade in the relevant HMC Capital Group Securities during that time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Escrowed or ASX-restricted units cannot be pledged, collared or sold at all until escrow ends, regardless of vesting status.

summary: A funded collar is workable here, and unusually well-supported by the drafting: HMC Capital Group Securities expressly includes Financial Products - covering options, swaps, CFDs and other derivatives related to the performance of HCW units - so a bank-written OTC put and call is itself ordinary Trading requiring the standard pre-approval process (written request to the Group CEO and Group Company Secretary, or the Chair/Company Secretary for a Director) rather than a definitional grey area. The loan leg needs separate prior consent from the Group CEO and Group Company Secretary (or the Chair, if either of them is the applicant) before a Director or Senior Executive enters a margin lending arrangement, includes the units in a margin loan portfolio, or transfers units into an existing margin account, and that consent may be made conditional (for example on the circumstances triggering a permitted margin-call sale). Critically, a secured lender's enforcement sale is excluded from the Blackout Period ban, but only if the underlying loan was not itself entered into in breach of section 8, and if the executive retains any control over which units are sold to meet a call, that sale needs its own prior consent. Hedging is only expressly banned for unvested incentive securities or those still subject to a holding lock, so a collar over already-vested, unrestricted units avoids that specific prohibition, subject to the ordinary Blackout Periods (1 January-half year results and 1 July-annual results, each plus one business day) and the 6-month short-term trading and short-position bans. Overall: proceed via GCEO/Company Secretary (or Chair) consent for both the loan and the derivative legs, executed outside Blackout Periods, with the loan's enforcement triggers cleared in advance to preserve the forced-sale exclusion.
